title: Trial of Toil
function: Usefulness, dignity, respect, responsibility, and the beginning of meaningful contribution.
sourceAuthority: current Trial of Toil development lock
released Issue 1 visual canon and Issues 2–5 current story continuity
dramaticRule: The support group is the catalyst and recurring relationship, not the container for the entire issue. Bjorn's change must be demonstrated in the apartment, neighborhood, and ordinary relationships as well as discussed inside the group.

bjornArc.setup: After Issue 5 shows the Vikings becoming known and cared for in their neighborhood, Bjorn becomes increasingly distressed by receiving care without an equivalent way to contribute. His old identity was built around providing, deciding, protecting, and carrying responsibility for other people.
bjornArc.rupture: Bjorn's attempt to prove he can still protect the household becomes a dangerous outburst inside the apartment. Carrie treats the behavior as a real risk rather than dismissing it as culture or frustration.
bjornArc.carrieAction: Carrie brings Bjorn to a DTI temporal-refugee support group.
bjornArc.groupConcept: The group is an ordinary ongoing support group containing temporal refugees displaced from widely different eras.
bjornArc.1980sParticipant: One participant is from the 1980s and resents being grouped with 'historical' refugees because they do not consider themselves very old. Their experience demonstrates that temporal displacement is not proportional to historical distance.
bjornArc.bjornParticipation: Bjorn takes the group unusually seriously. He listens as if people are bringing matters before council, notices contradictions, presses past evasions, and challenges the group leader intellectually because he is genuinely engaged.
bjornArc.groupLeader: The leader remains unnamed in this pass. They are competent and secure enough to challenge Bjorn back. Their intellectual friction becomes one of Bjorn's first modern relationships built on adult respect.
bjornArc.outsideApplication: The issue repeatedly cuts away from the group to ordinary life. Bjorn experiments with asking before taking responsibility, waits to be invited into work instead of seizing it, lets other people choose whether they want judgment or simple witness, and discovers that contribution can be reciprocal rather than compulsory.
bjornArc.emergentLeadership: Other participants begin valuing Bjorn's judgment and steadiness in small ways: asking what he thinks, answering when he asks a serious question, remembering something he said, noticing his absence, or taking strength from his presence. Bjorn learns to ask whether someone wants counsel or witness and begins functioning as a leader without becoming clinically responsible for the group.
bjornArc.needOne: Respect: the group leader treats Bjorn's thinking as worth arguing with.
bjornArc.needTwo: Meaning: other people begin to value Bjorn's presence and judgment without needing to obey him.
bjornArc.result: Bjorn accidentally thrives. His first meaningful modern contribution is leadership practiced through consent, attention, and responsibility rather than command.
bjornArc.employmentTrajectory: No job offer occurs in Issue 6. Later, the same strengths may grow naturally into paid peer support, temporal-refugee orientation, group assistance, or another non-clinical role built around lived experience and leadership.

pageSpine.title: Known Here
pageSpine.entry: Issue 5 neighborhood recognition is now ordinary.
pageSpine.turn: The Bodega Owner refuses Bjorn's attempt to make kindness into a settled debt.
pageSpine.exit: Belonging feels good and intolerably unearned at the same time.

pageSpine.title: No Empty Hands
pageSpine.entry: The Kin and Gunnar competently manage the household.
pageSpine.turn: Every useful task Bjorn reaches for is already handled, and Carrie arrives with more solved needs.
pageSpine.exit: Relief feels like erasure of his provider role.

pageSpine.title: A Job That Is Not Yours
pageSpine.entry: Bjorn sees a heavy bodega delivery as obvious useful work.
pageSpine.turn: The driver and owner need him to stop because the load is someone else's paid responsibility.
pageSpine.exit: 'Not your job' lands as 'there is no place for your strength.'

pageSpine.title: Provision
pageSpine.entry: Carrie confronts Bjorn's escalating restlessness.
pageSpine.turn: Bjorn finally names the wound: everyone else now carries the law, food, roads, and household competence.
pageSpine.exit: Carrie understands that his anger is about meaningful responsibility, not simple gratitude.

pageSpine.title: The Rupture
pageSpine.entry: A minor household electrical failure creates a real but contained hazard.
pageSpine.turn: After the danger is over, Bjorn loses control and smashes the dead power strip into the wall, frightening the Kin.
pageSpine.exit: Carrie names the behavior as dangerous and requires a change.

pageSpine.title: Not Punishment
pageSpine.entry: Carrie brings Bjorn to a DTI support-group door.
pageSpine.turn: She makes clear this is not a disciplinary or compliance hearing; the people inside understand displacement from their own lives.
pageSpine.exit: Bjorn enters by choice.

pageSpine.title: I Had a VCR
pageSpine.entry: Bjorn tries to classify the room by historical distance.
pageSpine.turn: A participant from 1987 rejects being treated as ancient and reveals that closeness in years does not make displacement easy.
pageSpine.exit: Bjorn stops sorting by era and starts listening to loss.

pageSpine.title: A Council Without Orders
pageSpine.entry: Bjorn expects rules, authority, and compelled testimony.
pageSpine.turn: The group leader establishes voluntary speech, passing, and consent as the room's operating structure.
pageSpine.exit: Bjorn stays because the boundary is stated without diminishing him.

pageSpine.title: Truth Is Not Owed
pageSpine.entry: A participant says they are fine while describing a life stripped of role and continuity.
pageSpine.turn: Bjorn correctly identifies the contradiction but corners the speaker; the leader stops him and distinguishes seeing truth from owning it.
pageSpine.exit: Bjorn is angry because the correction is intellectually serious rather than dismissive.

pageSpine.title: Worth the Argument
pageSpine.entry: Carrie waits outside after the first session.
pageSpine.turn: Bjorn emerges still arguing with the leader about whether useful questions may be refused.
pageSpine.exit: Carrie realizes he did not endure the group; he engaged with it.

pageSpine.title: The First Attempt
pageSpine.entry: Back at the Safe Cave, Gunnar and a Kin member disagree over a shared household object.
pageSpine.turn: Bjorn starts to rule automatically, stops, and awkwardly asks whether they want his decision or his judgment.
pageSpine.exit: They want his judgment. Authority becomes something requested rather than assumed.

pageSpine.title: Asked
pageSpine.entry: The same bodega delivery problem recurs in miniature.
pageSpine.turn: Bjorn waits instead of inserting himself; the owner then asks him for one specific piece of help.
pageSpine.exit: Being asked to help feels better than taking work from someone else.

pageSpine.title: A Hand Offered
pageSpine.entry: A Kin member is repairing or reorganizing something ordinary in the apartment.
pageSpine.turn: Bjorn offers help without taking over and accepts a limited role when invited.
pageSpine.exit: Contribution no longer requires being the only person capable of the task.

pageSpine.title: He Knows the Way
pageSpine.entry: Carrie arrives expecting to take Bjorn to the next session.
pageSpine.turn: He has already left; Gunnar helped him learn the route and Bjorn chose to go back on his own.
pageSpine.exit: The support group becomes Bjorn's relationship, not Carrie's compliance task.

pageSpine.title: Not Long Ago
pageSpine.entry: The 1980s participant jokes about modern technology before the session begins.
pageSpine.turn: They reveal that parents are dead, a younger sibling is now old, and everyone they knew lived decades without them.
pageSpine.exit: Bjorn names the shared wound as stolen sequence, not historical distance.

pageSpine.title: What Do You Want?
pageSpine.entry: A participant asks Bjorn whether to attend a descendant's family gathering.
pageSpine.turn: Instead of issuing a decision, Bjorn asks what outcome they want.
pageSpine.exit: His first question changes the advice that follows.

pageSpine.title: A Boundary, Not an Order
pageSpine.entry: The participant explains they want contact but not to be displayed as a historical curiosity.
pageSpine.turn: Bjorn offers a boundary and an exit rather than a command.
pageSpine.exit: His judgment matters without controlling the choice.

pageSpine.title: Work and Worth
pageSpine.entry: After the session, Bjorn argues that every adult needs work that matters.
pageSpine.turn: The leader agrees about meaningful contribution while refusing Bjorn's equation of usefulness with deserving care.
pageSpine.exit: Neither wins; the unresolved argument establishes genuine adult respect.

pageSpine.title: Ask First
pageSpine.entry: At home, a small dispute pulls Bjorn toward his old command reflex.
pageSpine.turn: He asks 'counsel or witness?' in language that sounds absurdly formal in the kitchen but gets a real answer.
pageSpine.exit: The household begins adapting to Bjorn's changed leadership instead of merely accommodating his old one.

pageSpine.title: Noticed
pageSpine.entry: Bjorn arrives late to a later group session because ordinary neighborhood life delayed him.
pageSpine.turn: The group has functioned without him but saved a question because his particular judgment is wanted.
pageSpine.exit: He is valued without becoming indispensable.

pageSpine.title: Witness
pageSpine.entry: A distressed participant arrives after a disastrous modern appointment and begins recounting it.
pageSpine.turn: Bjorn asks whether they want counsel or witness and honors the answer 'witness.'
pageSpine.exit: Disciplined attention becomes useful responsibility.

pageSpine.title: The Thing He Would Not Name
pageSpine.entry: After weeks of hearing other people, Bjorn volunteers his own problem.
pageSpine.turn: He admits that if nobody needs his protection he no longer knows why he is here.
pageSpine.exit: The leader offers a new model: a hand can be offered before it is required.

pageSpine.title: Something He Said
pageSpine.entry: Outside the formal group setting, the participant from Pages 16–17 reports back after the family dinner.
pageSpine.turn: They used Bjorn's boundary, left when displayed, and were invited back under better terms.
pageSpine.exit: Bjorn sees concrete proof that his judgment changed another life without controlling it.

pageSpine.title: Work That Matters
pageSpine.entry: Another ordinary session ends and people disperse into their separate lives.
pageSpine.turn: A participant asks Bjorn to return because they want his judgment; the leader confirms he is counted on but not required for the group to function.
pageSpine.exit: Outside, Carrie asks how it went. Bjorn answers: 'There is work here.'

issueBridge.issue6Question: What does Bjorn have to offer this place, and can contribution take a form he did not previously recognize as work?
issueBridge.towardIssue7: Bjorn enters War Council with leadership restored but altered: he can gather people and take responsibility without assuming that unity requires obedience or one answer.
issueBridge.towardFinale: The support-group arc establishes that Bjorn is not only being supported by New York; his presence matters to other people, and he has begun learning how to lead people whose choices remain their own.

boundaries.clinicalRole: Bjorn remains a participant and emerging peer leader, not a therapist or licensed clinician.
boundaries.groupDependence: Other participants value his leadership without becoming dependent on him.
boundaries.groupLeader: The group leader remains a capable counterpart rather than a foil for Bjorn to defeat; exact identity remains open until separately locked.
boundaries.participantRoster: Only the required 1980s participant is structurally fixed. Other participants remain unnamed temporal refugees so this pass does not silently lock an exact roster.
boundaries.employmentTiming: Employment follows later from established meaning and contribution rather than arriving as an immediate reward.
boundaries.groupScreenTime: Do not stage the back half as an uninterrupted sequence of therapy-room lessons. Each return to the group must change what Bjorn does in ordinary life, and ordinary life must in turn change what he brings back to the group.
boundaries.demotedMaterial: Community College and the old DMV chain are not forced into Issue 6; the current Master Project Bible supersedes that older normalization.
